marrow__ANAT_CH09_Q015.takeaway: The hypophysis cerebri develops from surface ectoderm (anterior lobe) and neuroectoderm (posterior lobe).
marrow__ANAT_CH09_Q015.displayText:
The hypophysis cerebri or pituitary gland develops from two sources i.e. surface ectoderm and neuroectoderm.

The adenohypophysis or anterior pituitary develops from the surface ectoderm. An ectodermal diverticulum, called Rathke's pouch, grows upward from the roof of the stomatodeum (primitive mouth). This becomes the anterior lobe of the pituitary (pars distalis).

The neurohypophysis or posterior pituitary develops from the neuroectoderm. A downward extension of the diencephalon, called infundibular process, grows down from the floor of the 3rd ventricle, during the 6th week. It gives rise to the stalk and the posterior lobe of pituitary (pars nervosa).

The anterior lobe of pituitary gives rise to a small extension called the pars tuberalis. It grows along the stalk of the infundibulum and eventually surrounds it.

The posterior wall of the Rathke pouch develops into the pars intermedia.

rationales.a: Surface ectoderm contributes to the adenohypophysis, but the second pituitary source is neuroectoderm rather than mesoderm.
rationales.c: Neuroectoderm forms the neurohypophysis, but the adenohypophysis arises from surface ectoderm rather than mesoderm.
rationales.d: Neither mesoderm nor endoderm is the source pair for the pituitary; the gland develops from surface ectoderm and neuroectoderm.

marrow__ANAT_CH09_Q016.takeaway: The pineal gland develops from the most caudal part of the diencephalic roof plate.
marrow__ANAT_CH09_Q016.displayText:
The pineal gland develops from the diencephalon. Hence, defect in its development can cause pineal agenesis.

The most caudal part of the roof plate of the diencephalon develops into the pineal gland. It is also known as the pineal body or epiphysis cerebri. The pineal body initially appears as an epithelial thickening in the midline. It begins to evaginate by the 7th week and becomes a solid organ.

rationales.a: The telencephalon forms the cerebral hemispheres and related forebrain structures; the pineal body arises from the diencephalic roof plate.
rationales.c: The metencephalon gives rise to the pons and cerebellum, whereas the pineal gland is a diencephalic derivative.
rationales.d: The myelencephalon forms the medulla oblongata; it does not give rise to the pineal gland.

marrow__ANAT_CH09_Q017.takeaway: The adrenal cortex is mesodermal, while the adrenal medulla is derived from neural crest cells.
marrow__ANAT_CH09_Q017.displayText:
The cells of the adrenal cortex and medulla are respectively derived from the mesoderm and neural crest cells.

The adrenal glands consist of a superficial cortex and deeper medulla.
• Adrenal cortex - formed by proliferation of the coelomic epithelium (mesodermal origin)
• Adrenal medulla - formed by the invading neural crest cells from somite levels 18-24

rationales.a: Neural crest correctly identifies the medullary source, but the cortex is mesodermal rather than ectodermal.
rationales.b: Mesoderm correctly identifies the cortical source, but the medulla comes from neural crest cells, not endoderm.
rationales.c: Neural crest correctly identifies the medulla, but the adrenal cortex is mesodermal rather than endodermal.

marrow__ANAT_CH09_Q018.takeaway: At birth, the zona glomerulosa and zona fasciculata are present; the zona reticularis forms later.
marrow__ANAT_CH09_Q018.displayText:
The zona glomerulosa and zona fasciculata of the adult cortex are present at birth.

The differentiation of the cortical zones of the adrenal gland begins during the late fetal period.
• Zona glomerulosa and zona fasciculata of the adult cortex are present at birth
• Zona reticularis is formed during the 3rd year of life

rationales.a: The zona fasciculata is present at birth, but the zona reticularis develops during the third year of life.
rationales.c: The zona glomerulosa is present at birth, but the zona reticularis is not yet formed.
rationales.d: This includes the zona reticularis, which forms during the third year; only the zona glomerulosa and zona fasciculata are present at birth.
